Missing Not At Random (MNAR).** Non-respondents ("No especificado") for several questions are structurally different from respondents, so the imputed marginal will always diverge from the observed marginal even with a perfect imputation model: | Column | N imputed | TV | Why non-respondents differ | |---|---|---|---| | `ENT_PAIS_NAC_CAT` | 459 | 0.882 | Likely migrants who preferred not to report birthplace | | `ENT_PAIS_RES_CAT` | 198 | 0.848 | People who did not live in Mexico 5 years ago | | `EDUC` | 1 253 | 0.844 | Atypical schooling (foreign credentials, indigenous education) | | `CONACT_CAT` | 2 716 | 0.560 | Marginal labour-force participants harder to classify | | `SITUA_CONYUGAL_CAT` | 153 | 0.519 | Uncommon partnership arrangements | | `DHSERSAL1` | 493 | 0.327 | Unaffiliated individuals less likely to identify a primary service | | `ASISTEN` | 316 | 0.274 | School-attendance edge cases (home-schooled, adult education) | These high TV values are expected and cannot be reduced without external calibration data. They do not indicate that the imputed values are wrong — only that the missing data is not a random subsample of the observed data. **2. Small-N sampling artefact.** Columns where TV > 0.05 but N < 50 (e.g. `CUADORM_CAT` N = 17, TV = 0.644; `TOTCUART_CAT` N = 21, TV = 0.422; `EDAD_CAT` N = 10, TV = 0.343) owe their high TV entirely to one or two imputed cells that happened to land in a rare category. With N = 17 a single flip gives TV = 1/17 = 0.059 — five flips gives TV = 0.29. These columns are functionally fully observed (< 0.01% of rows imputed) and the validation statistic is uninformative at this sample size. --- ## INGTRHOG_CAT Consistency `INGTRHOG` (total household labour income) equals the sum of `INGTRMEN` (monthly individual labour income) across all workers in the household. For the 490 households where `INGTRHOG_CAT` was imputed, the observed `INGTRMEN` values provide a hard lower bound: the imputed category's upper limit must be ≥ the observed sum. Violations are corrected deterministically by replacing the imputed category with the bin that contains the observed sum. ::: {#tbl-ingtrhog-repair .cell tbl-cap='INGTRHOG_CAT violations detected and repaired post-MICE' execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: --- ## Deterministic Imputation In deterministic mode each missing cell is assigned the **highest-probability class** (argmax) rather than a draw from the predicted distribution. This eliminates iteration-to-iteration sampling noise, making convergence faster and isolating the model's systematic bias from stochastic variance. The trade-off is that rare categories are systematically under-represented: the imputed marginals are pulled toward the modal class. ::: {#setup-det .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Deterministic outputs available: True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-det-setup .cell tbl-cap='Deterministic run parameters' execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Convergence (deterministic) Because the imputed value for each cell is a deterministic function of the training data, iteration-to-iteration TV reflects only how much the *models* change as other columns' imputed values are refined — not sampling noise. Convergence is therefore faster and cleaner: **28/40 columns converged** vs. 8/40 in the stochastic run, and mean final-gap TV fell from 0.059 to 0.009. The 12 still-non-converged columns fall into two groups. Ten have N < 200 imputed cells; for these the 1/N noise floor remains, though it is now driven by model instability rather than sampling variance. Two have larger N (`DHSERSAL1` N = 493, TV = 0.041; `ALFABET` N = 938, TV = 0.012) reflecting genuine residual model sensitivity to the changing imputed predictor values in each iteration. ::: {#tbl-det-convergence .cell tbl-cap='Deterministic run — TV distance between consecutive iterations' execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} if _det_available: _det_conv = pd.read_csv(_det_conv_path) _det_conv["table_col"] = _det_conv["table"] + " / " + _det_conv["column"] _dpivot = _det_conv.pivot_table(index="table_col", columns="iteration", values="tv_distance") _dsorted_iters = sorted(_dpivot.columns, key=_iter_key) _dpivot = _dpivot[_dsorted_iters] _dpivot["max_tv"] = _dpivot.max(axis=1) _dlast = _dsorted_iters[-1] _dpivot["converged"] = _dpivot[_dlast] < 0.01 _n_conv_det = int(_dpivot["converged"].sum()) _n_total = len(_dpivot) print(f"Converged (TV < 0.01 in final gap): {_n_conv_det}/{_n_total}") display(_dpivot.sort_values("max_tv", ascending=False).drop(columns="max_tv").style.format( "{:.3f}", subset=_dsorted_iters ).map( lambda v: "color: red" if isinstance(v, float) and v >= 0.01 else "", subset=[_dlast], )) else: print("⏳ Pending deterministic run.") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Converged (TV < 0.01 in final gap): 28/40 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

The model is confident enough that the argmax matches the plurality of stochastic draws — the divergence from observed is driven entirely by the structural difference between respondents and non-respondents, not by sampling noise. No amount of iterations or mode change will reduce this TV. **2. Stochastic worse (Δ > 0.05, green).** Columns where stochastic sampling was inflating TV: `CUADORM_CAT` (Δ = +0.30), `RADIO` (+0.09), `ALFABET` (+0.08), `RELIGION_CAT` (+0.09), `LAVADORA` (+0.07), `CISTERNA` (+0.08), `AUTOPROP` (+0.05). These are columns with moderate N (64–938) where occasional unlucky draws pulled the stochastic imputed marginal away from the predicted modal distribution. **3. Deterministic worse (Δ < −0.05, red).** `EDAD_CAT` (Δ = −0.36), `ELECTRICIDAD` (−0.36), `ENT_PAIS_RES_CAT` (−0.15), `BICICLETA` (−0.17), `MOTOCICLETA` (−0.10), `DHSERSAL1` (−0.14), `TINACO` (−0.12). For these columns argmax is over-confident: it always picks the dominant category, dramatically under-representing the minority categories that non-respondents actually belong to. Stochastic sampling spreads draws across categories in proportion to predicted probability and happens to produce distributions that are closer to observed. This is the canonical failure mode of deterministic MICE. ### Convergence — columns converged per mode ::: {#tbl-comparison-convergence .cell tbl-cap='Convergence summary: stochastic vs. deterministic' execution_count=17} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
